newsitem.title: USA: KCBT WHEAT SLIPS OFF HIGHS TO END STEADY TO LOWER.
newsitem.headline: KCBT WHEAT SLIPS OFF HIGHS TO END STEADY TO LOWER.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower after slipping off the earlier highs set on spillover support from corn, traders said.

Wheat gained early, pulled up by CBOT corn futures, which surged after USDA estimated corn production at 9.276 billion bushels--well below an average analyst estimate of 9.554 billion bushels and slightly smaller than last year's production of 9.293 billion.
"We went up with corn but slowly drifted back to trade actual value," a KCBT trader said. "It took us a while to shrug off corn's influence."
USDA's report also pegged U.S. wheat production at 2.531 billion bushels, which was above an average analysts' estimate of 2.476 billion bushels and last year's crop of 2.282 billion.
KCBT wheat settled 1/2 to 1-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with Sept wheat down 1-3/4 cents at $3.74-1/4. Earlier, Sept wheat had traded as high as $3.83, up seven cents on the day.

The main feature in Tuesday's session was heavy intra-market spreading by fund-related players, traders said. Chicago Corp bought 4.4 million bushels of the KCBT September/December spread at 13-1/2 to 14 cents.
E. D. & F. Man International bull-spread two million Sept/March bushels at 22 to 22-1/2 cents, floor sources said.
FIMAT bear-spread three million Dec/Sept in the same range, traders said, and Cargill Investor Services bear-spread at least one million Dec/Sept at 13-1/2 cents.
The KCBT estimated Tuesday's wheat futures volume at 54.775 million bushels, up sharply from 28.205 million Monday.
